correctness.rationale: Proof uses exact definition from Takahashi 2026, prior certified 4-person unsolvable classification, and a closed 6-person case analysis. Each 4-person unsolvable profile has 3 distinct singleton blocker sets, precluding BN domination by Takahashi Lemma 1. The six-person profile is unstabilizable because V is a cyclic triple that always supplies a blocker; 9 one-cross matchings are exactly the Pareto optima; after one adjacent U reversal, matching-edge cases 02,12,01 give respectively 3 BN,3 BN,3 Pareto but BN dominated, totaling 6 vs 9. The bundled Python code reconstructs all 1296 four-person profiles plus 15 matchings of each six-person witness; every asserted result passed. The result does not rely on extrapolation from sample data.

originality.rationale: Actual published-finding corpus queries for blocking-neutrality and the six/four-person comparison returned no covering finding; the closest published four-person result counts stable matchings, not blocking-neutrality. Takahashi 2026 full primary PDF was read at the definition, monotonicity, inclusion, stability-coincidence, and all examples: it proves general framework and displays other examples but not the exact conditional first-six separation or the one-swap 9-to-6 selective transition. A no-indexed-hit result alone would not suffice; novelty rests on nonimplication of those prior statements and this independently proved witness. Residual risk of unindexed earlier equivalent examples remains.

value.rationale: The first unsolvable compulsory-pairing market in which a stability fallback genuinely refines Pareto selection identifies a natural sharp boundary, and a single adjacent reversal alters the blocking-neutral set while leaving the no-stable status and the nine Pareto optima unchanged. This is a nontrivial link between instability and selection distinct from simple existence/efficiency statements; no all-six census or broad impossibility claim is made.
